subject: Request: short-term rate uplift & SLA addendum for upcoming product launch
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@fastretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short-term rate uplift & SLA addendum for upcoming product launch

Hi Mina / Ben,

We're rolling our new checkout experience on April 20 (soft launch) with a heavy burst expected during the first 72 hours. Forecasts attached (FastRetail_Surge_Specs.xlsx) show a 6–8x spike in token requests for 36–48 hours. Our legal/procurement team has asked whether Redwood can: 1) provide a short-term rate/quotas uplift for the launch window, and 2) sign a short SLA addendum that includes a latency SLO (99th-pct token latency) for that window and explicit fairness policy carveouts so our traffic isn't deprioritized by standard throttling rules.

We'd prefer to avoid an immediate Dedicated purchase but need predictable latency for the first 72 hours; if Redwood can offer a temporary uplift + an addendum, procurement can fast-track approval. Two quick Qs for you:
- Can you do a 48–72 hour controlled burst with an SLO addendum?
- If yes, how does billing/overage work for a temporary uplift?

I've copied procurement for any contract/compliance questions. Attached is the traffic forecast. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through details this week.

Thanks,
Emma Li
VP Product, FastRetail
emma.li@fastretail.com
(415) 555-0182

Attachment: FastRetail_Surge_Specs.xlsx
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term rate uplift & SLA addendum for upcoming product launch

Hi Emma — thanks for the data and heads-up, this is exactly the kind of scenario we plan for. Initial notes:

- Short answer: yes, we can support a controlled burst window with an SLA addendum in principle, but the exact terms depend on traffic shape and whether you can enable caching and other mitigations.
- Options we typically offer: transient burst upgrade (48–72h) with an explicit temporary quota uplift + a one-off SLA addendum covering latency during the window, or a short-term Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput.

To move quickly, can you confirm:
1) expected peak RPS and percent of requests that are purely generation vs embeddings/rerank;
2) whether you control client-side retries/backoff; and
3) acceptance of a canary rollout (we recommend a small pre-launch window to validate).

I've attached an SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx to show the language we typically use (non-binding until legal signs). Ben — can you and Karthik weigh in on capacity and estimated uplift cost? If acceptable, we can route a DocuSign for procurement next week.

Short call is fine — I'm available tomorrow 11:00–12:30 PT.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachment: SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term rate uplift & SLA addendum for upcoming product launch

Mina / Ben — did a quick capacity check with runtime team after reviewing the spreadsheet and traffic_graph_q2.png. Technical assessment summary:

- Feasibility: We can support a 48–72 hour burst of up to ~6x baseline peak on Hosted (multi-tenant) if FastRetail agrees to the following mitigations:
  * enable prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts (estimated 20–30% effective token reduction),
  * set an application-side retry/backoff policy to avoid synchronized retries,
  * restrict the burst window to a defined 48h block with a 2-hour canary period at 30% traffic before ramp.
- Fairness/Throttling: We will carve out a temporary priority policy for the burst window that elevates FastRetail requests above normal fairness tiers, but only within the provisioned uplift quota. Outside the uplift quota, standard rate limiting applies. This avoids impacting other customers.
- Latency SLO: We can commit to a provisional 99th-pct token latency target during the uplift window provided the canary passes and the traffic distribution matches the forecast. If observed latencies exceed the SLO, the plan includes automatic traffic shaping and a rollback to baseline quotas.
- Cost: Rough estimate is a one-time uplift surcharge equivalent to ~1.8x normal hosted overage rates for the uplifted tokens; exact number to confirm with billing.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Agree canary date and 48h window (we need fixed UTC bounds),
2) FastRetail enables caching and provides exact peak RPS and retry policy,
3) I’ll prepare a short runbook (failsafe triggers, escalation path, rollback steps) and attach traffic_graph_q2.png and a runbook link.

I put a draft runbook in the Redwood docs link below. If you want, we can spin up a small Dedicated pool as a fallback but that requires a minimum reservation and takes longer.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: traffic_graph_q2.png
Related: https://docs.redwood.ai/launch-runbook/FR-2027
From: Emma Li <emma.li@fastretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fastretail.com, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term rate uplift & SLA addendum for upcoming product launch

Thanks — that all sounds reasonable. Procurement reviewed the SLA_Addendum_Draft and asked for two clarifications (non-material): explicit UTC window and rollback triggers. We accept the 48h uplift with a 2h canary at 30% traffic.

Can we lock the window for April 20 00:00 UTC -> April 22 00:00 UTC with a canary on April 20 00:00–02:00 UTC? If you can provide the final addendum and a DocuSign link today or tomorrow, procurement will sign. Also confirm the uplift surcharge and final wording on the fairness carveout (we need a clause that we won't be deprioritized by cross-customer fairness policies within the uplifted quota).

If you send the DocuSign link we'll get procurement to countersign.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll enable prefix caching and share our retry/backoff config by EOD.

Emma
VP Product, FastRetail

Attachment: none
